cells.title: Assisted Solo Demonstration
cells.description: Demonstration of a series of Assisted Solo exercises created by Hauert and Zoo Company to short circuit habitual patterns of coordination through external inputs. Video starts with a demonstration of Light Touches and then the Pressure and Loose Impulse exercises. Dancers: Thomas Hauert, Sara Ludi, Mat Voorter

cells.title: Attentive Agent, Light Touches
cells.description: Contact at body joints causes localized adjustments and movement is isolated. The body adapts to overlapping actions.

cells.title: Assisted Solo Performance, Mixed Strategies
cells.description: Thomas performs the assisted solo exercise using the Pressure strategy first. He then adds momentum to move into a mix of Pressure and Loose Impulse approaches by receiving and responding to inputs. Dancers: Thomas Hauert, Sara Ludi, Mat Voorter

cells.title: Assisted Solo Performances, Mixed Responses
cells.description: Assisted Solo performances in which a soloist receives external impulses from two assistants and uses a mix of different possible responses. Finally, the soloist continues the dance alone, recalling the timing and coordination of the inputs received. Dancers: Thomas Hauert, Sara Ludi, Mat Voorter

cells.title: Assisted Solos by All Three Dancers, Loose Impulse
cells.description: Dancers switch roles in this ongoing relay of Loose Impulse Assisted Solos. This strategy adds momentum to the mix and the soloist is letting all the imposed forces and directions combine in the body and is prolonging and suspending them slightly while waiting for the next input. Dancers: Thomas Hauert, Sara Ludi, Mat Voorter

cells.title: Mixed Roles Group Form, Performance 1
cells.description: Mixed Roles performance from an early Motion Bank residency with Zoo Company with Samantha van Wissen performing. This more complex Assisted Solo game makes everyone both assistant and soloist, creating a network of reactions and "one body out of many." Dancers: Thomas Hauert, Sara Ludi, Samantha van Wissen

cells.title: Attentive Agent, Pressure
cells.description: Assistants touch multiple places simultaneously while the soloist pushes back and contact points move through space.

cells.title: Attentive Agent, Mixed Roles
cells.description: Dancers push multiple places on each other and resist where they are pushed. Contact points also move through space.

cells.title: Mixed Roles Group Form, Performance 2
cells.description: The Mixed Roles Group Form is a more complex development of the Assisted Solos approach in which everyone acts as both soloist and assistant at the same time, giving and receiving inputs. Shot in slow-motion. Dancers: Thomas Hauert, Sara Ludi, Mat Voorter

cells.title: Impulse Body Text 1
cells.description: Assisted Solos are a creative tool and training exercise Thomas Hauert and Zoo Company have been using over the years.  In Assisted Solos, partners or assistants provide external impulses for a soloist in a series of different improvisation strategies from the introductory Light Touches to more complex forms involving several people and changing roles.

additional_fields.text-content: Assisted Solos are a creative tool and training exercise Thomas Hauert and Zoo Company have been using over the years. In Assisted Solos, partners or assistants provide external impulses for a soloist in a series of different improvisation strategies from the introductory Light Touches to more complex forms involving several people and changing roles.

cells.title: Impulse Call Out Text 1
cells.description:
“For a dancer, receiving impulses from assistants provides the experience of spontaneous and unpredictable strings and combinations of movements and requires an alert state of attention that is constantly traveling through the body. With practice, this alert attention and the unpredictable coordinations can be continued without the assistants.”
----- Thomas Hauert

additional_fields.html-content:
“For a dancer, receiving impulses from assistants provides the experience of spontaneous and unpredictable strings and combinations of movements and requires an alert state of attention that is constantly traveling through the body. With practice, this alert attention and the unpredictable coordinations can be continued without the assistants.”
----- Thomas Hauert

cells.title: Impulse Body Text 2
cells.description: The Assisted Solo strategies work to short-circuit habitual patterns of coordination. They also challenge the dancers to maintain a state of readiness, scanning constantly to respond to several simultaneous inputs and external impulses. This results in a special form of concentration that is evident when you watch them perform.

additional_fields.text-content: The Assisted Solo strategies work to short-circuit habitual patterns of coordination. They also challenge the dancers to maintain a state of readiness, scanning constantly to respond to several simultaneous inputs and external impulses. This results in a special form of concentration that is evident when you watch them perform.

cells.title: Impulse Body Text 3
cells.description: In the simplest form of an Assisted Solo, the assistants give Light Touches to the joints of the soloist to indicate where the next modification is to happen; the soloist determines the direction and amplitude of the movement they make in response.

additional_fields.text-content: In the simplest form of an Assisted Solo, the assistants give Light Touches to the joints of the soloist to indicate where the next modification is to happen; the soloist determines the direction and amplitude of the movement they make in response.

cells.title: Impulse Body Text 5
cells.description: One specific form of Assisted Solo is the Pressure exercise. Here, two assistants offer any possible part of their bodies as surfaces for the soloist to resist against. The task for the soloist is to respond with resistance to all the surfaces in contact with her. All parties involved can vary the pressure on those surfaces that create movement. It is a dynamic system relying on interactions between the three dancers.

additional_fields.text-content: One specific form of Assisted Solo is the Pressure exercise. Here, two assistants offer any possible part of their bodies as surfaces for the soloist to resist against. The task for the soloist is to respond with resistance to all the surfaces in contact with her. All parties involved can vary the pressure on those surfaces that create movement. It is a dynamic system relying on interactions between the three dancers.

cells.title: Impulse Call Out Text 4
cells.description:
“An important element of the assisted solo is falling and catching and trusting instability. The interaction with gravity as a source of force and direction makes gravity feel like a third assistant in these exercises.”
----- Thomas Hauert

additional_fields.html-content:
“An important element of the assisted solo is falling and catching and trusting instability. The interaction with gravity as a source of force and direction makes gravity feel like a third assistant in these exercises.”
----- Thomas Hauert

cells.title: Impulse Body Text 7
cells.description: A still more complex form of Assisted Solo is the Mixed Strategies dance, in which several types of touches and impulses are combined to create a more dynamic dance.  A Mixed Strategies dance may include controlled Pressure interactions, but also impulses where momentum is passed from the assistant to the soloist.  Tension and tension-release are two other parameters that come into the game: letting a force move you, modifying it, or resisting it.

cells.description:
“In these group forms it is as if we are creating one body out of many.”
----- Thomas Hauert

cells.title: Assisted Solo, Mixed Strategies (Motion Capture)
cells.description: The Assisted Solo strategy works to short circuit habitual patterns of coordination by giving a solo dancer several external impulses from assistant dancers. The exercise emphasizes the inputs and actions of the soloist but, as this motion capture data shows, the assistants' motion also reveals interesting patterns. Dancers: Thomas Hauert and Mat Voorter

cells.title: Assisted, Solo Pressure (Motion Capture)
cells.description: In this motion capture data, you are able to see the soloist alone and then watch the results of the input from assistants on the soloist's actions. Assisted Solos are a creative tool and training exercise Zoo Company uses where partners or assistants determine the chain of places where motion can happen in the actions of a soloist. Dancer: Sara Ludi

cells.title: Impulse Body Text 9
cells.description: The Assisted Solo exercise can become an even more complex game when the roles of assistants and soloist are not split anymore, but instead everyone takes on both roles at the same time, creating a network of chain-reactions and impulses.

additional_fields.text-content: The Assisted Solo exercise can become an even more complex game when the roles of assistants and soloist are not split anymore, but instead everyone takes on both roles at the same time, creating a network of chain-reactions and impulses.

cells.title: Impulse Call Out Text 5
cells.description:
“It is exhilarating and liberating the way the body keeps finding solutions to the most complex and unpredictable cocktails of forces and directions imposed on it.”
----- Thomas Hauert

additional_fields.html-content:
“It is exhilarating and liberating the way the body keeps finding solutions to the most complex and unpredictable cocktails of forces and directions imposed on it.”
----- Thomas Hauert

cells.title: Impulse Body Text 6
cells.description: In the Loose Impulse strategy, instead of holding, resisting, or applying pressure, the soloist allows all of the imposed forces and directions to combine in her body and then prolongs them, slighting and suspending them while waiting for the next input.

additional_fields.text-content: In the Loose Impulse strategy, instead of holding, resisting, or applying pressure, the soloist allows all of the imposed forces and directions to combine in her body and then prolongs them, slighting and suspending them while waiting for the next input.

cells.title: Impulse Call Out Text 2
cells.description:
“Once momentum is added, the soloist is being pushed and pulled off balance all the time, which constantly changes the situation of the body in relation to the floor. The speed of the interactions between all the motors and other elements involved doesn’t allow for very much conscious control.”
----- Thomas Hauert

additional_fields.html-content:
“Once momentum is added, the soloist is being pushed and pulled off balance all the time, which constantly changes the situation of the body in relation to the floor. The speed of the interactions between all the motors and other elements involved doesn’t allow for very much conscious control.”
----- Thomas Hauert

cells.title: Impulse Call Out Text 3
cells.description:
“For the soloist, many parameters stay open, meaning that there is space for creativity or, even, creativity is required for it to work.”
----- Thomas Hauert

additional_fields.html-content:
